Here's a version that brings in that contrast between where you were and where you are now:

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="64782"}
Spring in Tennessee hits a little differently this year.

This time last year, I was walking through one of the hardest seasons of my life. I felt depleted, exhausted, heartbroken, and honestly, there were moments when it felt like the world I had built was coming to an end.

The future felt uncertain. The road ahead felt impossible to see.

And yet, here we are.

Standing in a garden full of life, watching things bloom that started as tiny seeds months ago. Every flower, every vegetable, every bit of growth feels like a reminder that difficult seasons don't last forever.

As I look around at everything we've planted together, I can't help but see my own journey reflected in it.

Growth doesn't happen overnight. Neither does healing.

Some of the most important work happens underground, unseen, while roots are being established for what comes next.

Today, instead of fear, I see possibility.

Instead of loss, I see love.

Instead of wondering how I'll make it through, I find myself excited about what lies ahead.

And one of the greatest gifts of this season has been having someone beside me who chooses to grow alongside me. Someone willing to hold my hand through the difficult parts, celebrate the victories, and help build a future rooted in faith, hope, and purpose.

A year ago, I could never have imagined the peace I feel today.

Now all I see is life. Love. Growth. And a future full of amazing things still to come. 🌱❤️
:::

Here's a more reflective, hopeful version that ties your garden to your personal journey:

:::writing{variant="social_post" id="58241"}
There is something about springtime in Tennessee that feels a little like grace.

Everywhere I look, things are growing. Flowers pushing through the soil. Trees coming back to life. Tiny seeds becoming something beautiful with enough sunlight, patience, and care.

As I stand in this garden we've built, I can't help but see the parallels to my own life.

The last few years have stretched me in ways I never expected. There were seasons of loss, uncertainty, heartbreak, and rebuilding. Seasons where growth was happening beneath the surface long before anyone could see it.

And now, much like this garden, I can finally see new life emerging.

One of the greatest gifts of this season has been having someone beside me who isn't afraid of the hard parts. Someone willing to roll up his sleeves, get his hands dirty, and help tend to what is being rebuilt. Someone who chooses growth alongside me, even when the process isn't easy.

This garden isn't perfect. Neither am I.

But both are living proof that beautiful things can grow after difficult seasons.

The flowers remind me that healing is possible. The fresh blooms remind me that endings often make room for new beginnings. And every new leaf feels like a small reminder that who I was is not who I have to remain.

Spring has always been about rebirth.

This year, I think it's about becoming.

And for the first time in a very long time, I'm excited for what's growing next. 🌱💛
:::
